RADSC 101: Radiology history, basic radiation protection principles, medical terminology, introduction to radiography and radiographic procedures/lab.
RADSC 102: Continuation of Radiographic Procedures/Lab I to include finish appendicular skeleton, axial skeleton and introduction to skull anatomy and positioning.
RADSC 103: Continuation of Radiographic Procedures/Lab II to include digestive, urinary, and biliary systems and facial bone work.
RADSC 110: This course includes the basic concepts of patient care, including consideration for the physical and psychological needs of the patient and the family.
RADSC 204: This course establishes a knowledge base in factors that govern and influence the production and recording of radiographic images.
RADSC 205: This course is a continuation of Radiographic Exposure I, with emphasis on electronic imaging, image formation, quality assurance, & related areas.
RADSC 206: Emphasis on specialized positioning and advanced radiographic procedures; includes introduction to cross-sectional anatomy.
RADSC 207: Registry Review includes material from all radiological science courses, with emphasis on National Certification Examination, and career planning.
RADSC 210W: RADSC 210W Radiographic Pathology (3) A writing-intensive study of the basic fundamentals of pathology (disease process) with emphasis placed on radiographic presentation.
RADSC 220: Study the principles of interaction of radiation with living systems, effects on cells and tissues, biological response, and radiation protection.
RADSC 230: Basic knowledge of atomic structure, characteristics of radiation, x-ray production, photon interactions, circuitry, imaging equipment and quality control.
RADSC 295A: Supervised off-campus, non-group instruction including field experiences, practica, or internships.

RADSC 295D: Supervised off-campus group instruction including field experiences, practica, or internships.
RADSC 295E: Supervised off-campus, nongroup instruction including field experiences, practica, or internships.
RADSC 295F: Supervised off-campus, non-group instruction including field experiences, practica, or internships.
RADSC 295G: Supervised clinical education activities under the direction of registered radiologic technologists.
